answer: A pigment vertex survey stops a clone farm at the ridge. The claimant plants three pigment-marked posts as a triangle on a named ridge and photographs a comet crossing it on a fixed night. Two survey wardens re-measure the angles, match the pigment to the registry, and confirm the photograph against the comet's published path within five days. A copied triangle or mismatched pigment voids the season, burns a 160-credit stake, and bars the sponsor two years. One honest triangle costs a season of surveying; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 triangles planted, painted, and photographed by hand.
